criterion: Boundary values / wrong result: the check must refuse when the harness would ask (SDD §8 row "Spawn permission check"; contract Acceptance bullet 5)
finding: On Windows the check counts the main checkout's .claude/settings.local.json as a file Claude Code reads for a session in a linked worktree, but on Windows Claude Code does not read it. A rule found only there gives a false ok.
why: The Claude Code settings page (code.claude.com/docs/en/settings, "Where Claude Code keeps the local file in a git repository", read 2026-10-20) says a worktree session uses the main checkout's local file, then qualifies that: "When the file stays with `.claude/settings.json` instead: outside a git repository, when the repository root is your home directory, on Windows, ...". So on Windows the harness reads only <worktree>/.claude/settings.local.json. The plan's own trial agrees: copying the main checkout's local settings into a new worktree cleared the MCP dialog (SDD.md:1044, T10). The SDD requires the contact session to sit in a linked worktree (SDD §5 row "Write repository configuration"). Failing input: Windows; the contact session is in worktree W; the user settings file, W/.claude/settings.json and W/.claude/settings.local.json lack the rule; <main>/.claude/settings.local.json allows it. The check answers {ok: true, says: "the spawn rule is in <main>/.claude/settings.local.json permissions.allow"}, but the harness asks before the first transport command, which is the refusal AUTO-2 exists to prevent.
fix: Have afk_claude_spawn_rule_files print the main checkout's local file only where the harness reads it: not on Windows, not when the repository root is the home directory, and not outside git. Alternatively, drop it and print the repository-root local file under the documented rules. Fix the PROVIDERS.md:181 row to match, and add a test with the rule only in the main checkout's file under a Windows-shaped run.
evidence: claude.sh:88-89 `main=$(git -C "$root" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null) || return 0` / `printf '%s\n' "${main%/.git}/.claude/settings.local.json"`; claude.sh comment: "Settings files whose permission lists this harness reads for a session in $1"; SDD.md:1044 "Copying the main checkout's git-ignored local settings into a new worktree cleared the MCP dialog (T10)"

criterion: Acceptance: a rule that no longer matches after a plugin update makes the run refuse, naming the rule; H15 Probe contract: the refusal's `says` names the rule, the settings file and the list
finding: The `stale` refusal always names the first settings file (the user file) as the holder of the stale entry, wherever that entry really is. `stale` collects entry texts with no path, and the message uses `target = adapter["files"][0]`.
why: A stale entry in `<root>/.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json` produces 'the user file holds `<entry>`; replace it'. The human edits a file that does not hold the entry, the probe stays `stale`, and the H15 promise that `says` names the settings file is false on this path.
fix: Record (path, entry) pairs in `stale` and name the file that holds `stale[0]` in the message; add a test that puts a stale entry in the project or local file and asserts that path is in `says`.
evidence: permission.py:74 `stale += [e for e in entries if ENTRY_NAME in e and e != rule]`; :78 `target = adapter["files"][0] if adapter["files"] else "the user settings file"`; :86 `return _refuse(provider, rule, "stale", f"{target} {allow_key} holds `{stale[0]}`, which is not the current "`; MANIFEST.md:384 `names the rule, the settings file and the list.`

criterion: Acceptance: check() returns ok, or a refusal carrying the rule text (SDD §8); the refusal names the rule and /afk:setup (SDD §9b)
finding: The provider-layer refusal (no bash found, a bash timeout, or a nonzero adapter exit) returns `rule: ""`. Its `says` is the raw error, which names neither the rule nor /afk:setup.
why: SDD §8 fixes the interface as 'ok, or a refusal carrying the rule text', and §9b says every refusal names the rule and `/afk:setup`. This branch is a refusal that does neither, so a run refused here gives the human no route to a fix.
fix: Keep any `rule` the adapter printed before it failed, and append a pointer to /afk:setup to the provider-layer `says`. Add a test that stubs `run` to fail and asserts that /afk:setup is in `says`.
evidence: permission.py:53-54 `if "error" in adapter:` / `return _refuse(adapter.get("provider", "unknown"), "", "provider-layer", adapter["error"], [])`; contract Acceptance: `check() returns ok, or a refusal carrying the rule text`

criterion: Acceptance: the check confirms the harness will let the contact agent run the team entry script for all six verbs, and refuses, naming the rule, when it will not (SDD §8)
finding: The adapter's settings-file list leaves out managed (policy) settings. A managed deny or ask entry for the rule, or a managed policy that ignores user allow rules, makes the harness ask, but the check still answers ok. D-77 settles exact-text matching but does not cover managed settings.
why: The vendor permissions page says managed settings 'user and project settings can't override', and 'deny rules from any scope are evaluated before allow rules'. On a machine with a managed policy, the check passes, and the run is then refused at its first transport verb: the failure the check exists to prevent. Inferred: reachable only on machines with managed settings; not live-verified.
fix: Add the managed-settings path(s) to `afk_claude_spawn_rule_files` with their block lists (and an allow-only-managed flag if the adapter can express it), or record a decision that excludes managed settings and state the gap in PROVIDERS.md "Spawn allow rule".
evidence: claude.sh:86-89 `printf '%s\n' "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-${HOME:-}/.claude}/settings.json" (line continues) "$root/.claude/settings.json" "$root/.claude/settings.local.json"` then the main checkout's settings.local.json, and no managed file; code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (read 2026-10-20): `administrators deploy managed settings that user and project settings can't override` and `deny rules from any scope are evaluated before allow rules`

criterion: blast radius: a global, un-namespaced constant sourced into every hook shell
finding: AFK_SPAWN_ALLOW_RULE is the only top-level assignment in a provider adapter, and its name has no provider prefix. provider.sh sources every adapter into one shell for every hook, so a second adapter that defines the same constant silently replaces Claude's.
why: PROVIDERS.md tells adapter authors that afk_<name>_spawn_allow_rule 'prints the one constant AFK_SPAWN_ALLOW_RULE'. That invites the next harness that needs a rule to reuse the name. Adapters are sourced in glob order, so afk_claude_spawn_allow_rule would then print the other harness's rule, and both setup and the check would offer and verify the wrong text. Every other symbol in claude.sh is afk_claude_*-scoped.
fix: Scope the name to the provider. Either assign it as a local inside afk_claude_spawn_allow_rule (this keeps the Produces anchor token), or name it per provider and update the PROVIDERS.md row and the test's _constant regex.
evidence: claude.sh:77 `AFK_SPAWN_ALLOW_RULE='Bash(afk-python "${AFK_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/afk-team.py" *)'`; hooks/lib/provider.sh:13-16 `for afk_adapter in "$AFK_PROVIDER_CORE_DIR"/providers/*.sh; do ... . "$afk_adapter"`; PROVIDERS.md:180 `prints the one constant AFK_SPAWN_ALLOW_RULE`; git grep 'AFK_[A-Z_]*=' hooks/lib/providers/*.sh: only claude.sh:77

finding: No test reaches the fourth settings file, the main checkout's .claude/settings.local.json, which afk_claude_spawn_rule_files finds through git. The fixture's repo folder is never a git repository, so the git lookup always fails and the function returns after three files.
why: A contact agent working in a linked worktree may hold the rule only in the main checkout's settings.local.json. That path, and the `${main%/.git}` strip, could break without any test failing. Inferred from reading: the fixture never runs `git init`, and a probe of the default pytest temp root printed `fatal: not a git repository`. Because git searches parent folders, the lookup can also read a real repository's settings file. That happens when tmp_path sits inside a repository (a --basetemp under the repo) or when GIT_DIR is inherited.
fix: Add a case that creates a git repository and a linked worktree under tmp_path, puts RULE only in the main checkout's .claude/settings.local.json, runs the check from the worktree and asserts ok. Isolate the fixture env too: drop GIT_* variables and set GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=tmp_path.
evidence: test: `@pytest.mark.parametrize("where", ["user", "project", "local"])`; fixture: `config, repo = tmp_path / "config", tmp_path / "repo"` (no git init); claude.sh:88 `main=$(git -C "$root" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null) || return 0`

finding: No test covers the fail-closed branch, where the provider layer errors and the answer is a `provider-layer` refusal. That branch is reached by a bash exit other than 0, an OSError, a TimeoutExpired, or no POSIX shell. check_spawn_permission takes an injectable `run` parameter for exactly this, but no test passes it.
why: This branch decides whether a broken provider layer refuses or lets the run start. A regression could make it answer ok, or drop the error, and every current test would still pass. A grep for `run=` and `provider-layer` in scripts/tests found only the production definition.
fix: Add tests that pass a fake `run` which (a) raises subprocess.TimeoutExpired, (b) returns returncode 2 with stderr text, and (c) returns returncode 2 after printing a `provider	claude` line. Assert ok is False, problem == 'provider-layer' and that `says` carries the stderr text or exit code.
evidence: permission.py:50 `run: Callable = subprocess.run) -> dict:`; :54 `return _refuse(adapter.get("provider", "unknown"), "", "provider-layer", adapter["error"], [])`; test helper `return permission.check_spawn_permission(home["repo"], env=home["env"])` (never passes run)

finding: Possible conditional logic in a test: the _matches helper is a hand-written model of the harness's wildcard matcher with three branches. Every rule the tests pass ends in one trailing ` *`, so only the last branch decides any assertion. The `:*` branch and the general multi-`*` regex never run, and nothing tests them.
why: The claim that the rule covers all six verbs, and the start-only negative case, both rest on this model, not on the harness. The untested branches suggest the model covers more cases than it has shown. A later test using a multi-`*` or `:*` rule would trust code no test has run.
fix: Reduce _matches to the one form used (a single trailing ` *`) and assert that precondition, or add direct tests for the other branches. Keep the live proof in providers/CONFORMANCE.md as the authority.
evidence: `if pattern.endswith(":*"):` / `regex = ".*".join(re.escape(part) for part in pattern.split("*"))` / `if pattern.endswith(" *") and pattern.count("*") == 1:` then `regex = re.escape(pattern[:-2]) + "(?: .*)?"`

finding: The unreadable-file test proves the skip only by checking that one path string is absent. The bash side forms that string with `cygpath -m` and the test forms it with `.replace("\\", "/")`. If the two forms ever differ (an 8.3 short name, drive-letter case, a symlinked temp folder), the `not in` passes even when the file was not skipped.
why: A check that something is absent passes trivially when the strings differ in form. The test never shows that its path form appears in `files` at all.
fix: Assert the exact read list: `len(answer["files"]) == 1 and answer["files"][0].endswith(".claude/settings.local.json")`, or compare Path(...).resolve() values.
evidence: `assert answer["ok"] is True and str(home["user"]).replace("\\", "/") not in answer["files"]`

finding: One CLI test checks four behaviours in sequence: plain `rule` text, `rule --json`, `check` refusing with exit 1, and `check` passing with exit 0 after a settings file is written partway through.
why: A failure in the first assert hides the other three, and the name does not say which one broke.
fix: Split it into tests for `rule` output and for `check` exit codes, or parameterize it.
